claims.summary: Cornell describes Russian past forms as suffix -л- plus gender/number endings agreeing with the nominative subject; its table of contents contrasts this with person inflection in the non-past.
Cornell gives masculine Саша передал икру, feminine Маша передала икру, neuter вино стояло на столе, and plural Саша и Маша пили вино as past-tense examples.
The four Russian past-tense sentences and their gender/number readings are reproduced from Cornell’s examples.
The article confines its claim to the stated past/non-past inflection contrast and makes no inference about pronoun omission, irregular verbs, or every past-tense use.
